svg.title: Metaverse architecture: local execution and independent services
svg.desc: Three deployment lanes show a local user's Client, independent provider roles, and other participants' Clients. Each Client contains trusted Core and System UI, validation and storage support, isolated World Runtimes with Avatar and Item behavior sandboxes, independent Overlay Apps, and Client-owned brokers and platform adapters. All external communication crosses a Client-owned Network Broker. Resource Hosts and Mirrors provide immutable Release data; a Resource Relay fetches that data or accepts a local user's upload, then delivers it to other viewers. Separate session coordination, message, media, and optional authoritative backend roles exchange data through the same broker boundary. Optional directory, account and social, store and rights, and moderation services remain independent. Boxes describe logical roles, not mandatory operating-system processes; arrows show communication, not authority or inherited permissions.
svg.text: Content is downloaded; running copies are isolated locally; selected services connect participants.
Concept architecture · A possible online deployment, not a required process layout or universal network topology
Your chosen Client · local trust and permission boundary
Roles may share an operator, host, or deployment.
Their Clients enforce their own policy.
Principals · lifecycle · grants · budgets · safety controls
Trusted prompts and indicators stay outside application control.
Verify Releases; isolate parsers, decoders and compilers.
Content cache ≠ retained archive ≠ a running instance.
No arbitrary player or state control
Separate scopes and quotas, not inherited grants
Scoped host API requests; checked before access
Files · identity · storage · devices · tracking · audio
Narrow handles, revocation, lifecycle and quota checks
Native graphics, input, audio, devices and networking
Client / OS composition and safety remain in control.
Worlds, Avatars and Items may ship code.
A participant's code never receives your device permissions
merely because that participant joined the same session.
Published Release data, not running Worlds
Publication authority belongs to the Publisher, not the host.
fetch from remote source on cache miss
Accept local uploads OR fetch remote Content Files.
Validate admission limits; optionally cache; serve viewers.
Viewers do not contact participant-selected origins directly.
File delivery does not itself verify usage rights or grant execution.
Create / discover sessions; handle the join flow.
Not a required global coordinator or content authority.
Poses, events and bounded World messages
Optional Replication Policy: recipients, rate, detail
Separate media handling; not a Resource file host.
Own selected state domains; validate outcomes; persist data.
World-specific protocol or an opted-in Session Profile
Services are selected according to the experience.
A local / offline World needs no session provider.
Brokered discovery, account, commerce and policy calls
Independent providers; access is explicit, not a privilege inherited by World content.
Arrows show data flow / exchange, not authority.
Containers are logical boundaries, not mandatory OS processes or inherited grants.
No direct participant-to-participant connection is assumed.
